title: Liberal arts studies and writing arrangements by ear
summary: He studied liberal arts, never formally arranging, and worked out parts by ear and chord names.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: What were you studying at Bucknell?

Just a simple arts course, liberal arts. Liberal arts, to get through. Oh, I took Latin, I had several languages. Latin, French. I don't know why I supposed they all helped. I was rubbing elbows. It was the popular thing to go to school in those days.
But you hadn't yet really started studying arranging.
Oh, no. This is all-- what was it Churchill said, "picking up a few things as I go along." Well, yeah, but where I got that was I still knew about my harmonies

and so forth and liking -- I liked harmony better than anything. And so I had four instruments that first year to deal with, so I would write out the two-part harmony and then the other two parts, the trumpet and the trombone, I would have to put them together to get an ensemble, and the way I would accomplish this was I would write out the parts, put a piece over here and then write out the other part and maybe look back to see what I did once in awhile and I would do it all by ear.

And of course, the piano and the guitar parts were the names of the chords. Now, at this time we still had no bottom in the band. The drummer I never bothered with him because he couldn't drum anyway. All he could do was keep a little time with us, most of them was some guy that had a set of drums. He'd have brushes and he would play a little bit on the drums. On the drums, he you better not play. It was mostly on the cymbals and a little bit wire brush.

Well, there were woodblocks there too, but not so much there as when I played around Wilkes Barre. That was a city. They had several theatres and they were more apt to pick up the legitimate. We had good legitimate drummers there. But in college, you know, you just pick up some guy that brings a set of drums or the one guy bought a set of drums just so he could play in the band.
We never paid too much attention to him, just so he
didn't get in the way and then occasionally he'd like to hit the cymbal once in awhile in an open spot, so that went along in the second year.
